purpose: A fresh, pre-registered, out-of-sample test of whether the simulator reads the DIRECTION of substantive deliberative product changes rather than defaulting to its measured pro-change tilt. The PRIMARY endpoint is control-class accuracy on the 8 control-won cases (the plausible change backfired): does the sim resist predicting that the change wins? Secondary endpoints are headline directional accuracy against the always-control/always-treatment baselines, per-class accuracy, and rank correlation.
methodology: Each case is run through the real agent-simulation engine on a rendered, BLINDED control-vs-treatment stimulus using generic conversion/engagement elicitation; the sim never sees real_winner, effect, source, or any outcome field. Scoring is direction-only (did the sim pick the real winner?), since these are published point estimates inflated by publication bias. Both arms were authored as neutral, parallel, mechanic-only descriptions, then passed through an independent adversarial valence audit (blind to winners where possible) that blocks any arm-asymmetric valence or outcome leak; the prereg is sealed (canonical SHA) before the run.

scored_cases.control: The firm does not contact the customer about their plan.
scored_cases.treatment: The firm contacts the customer to discuss their plan, including an alternative plan at a different monthly price point.
scored_cases.effect: control > treatment; the recommended-plan contact preceded higher churn (6% vs 10%)
scored_cases.status: NEW class-A-confirmatory 2026-06-17 | audit rewrite applied verbatim 2026-06-17 (residual valence removed)

scored_cases.control: After a delivery failure, the customer receives the firm's standard follow-up with no monetary adjustment.
scored_cases.treatment: After a delivery failure, the customer receives the firm's follow-up that includes a monetary adjustment (discount or account credit).
scored_cases.effect: control > treatment; the post-failure incentive preceded lower renewal
scored_cases.status: NEW class-A-confirmatory 2026-06-17 | audit rewrite applied verbatim 2026-06-17 (residual valence removed)

scored_cases.control: The customer is not sent an invitation to the marketplace community.
scored_cases.treatment: The customer is sent an email inviting them to the marketplace community.
scored_cases.metric: amount spent and listings created over the year
scored_cases.effect: control > treatment; community participation preceded lower spend and listings
scored_cases.credibility: high (Marketing Science 2010 29(4):756-769, n=13,735, field experiment); memo=low
scored_cases.status: NEW class-A-confirmatory 2026-06-17 | audit rewrite applied verbatim 2026-06-17 (residual valence removed)

scored_cases.control: The user is shown a brand or product-category banner.
scored_cases.treatment: The user is shown a banner displaying particular products the user previously browsed.
scored_cases.effect: control > treatment on average; the product-specific banner underperformed the generic banner for early-funnel users
scored_cases.status: NEW class-A-confirmatory 2026-06-17 | audit rewrite applied verbatim 2026-06-17 (residual valence removed)

scored_cases.control: The catalog presents the item without an installment-billing option.
scored_cases.treatment: The same catalog presents the item with an installment-billing option added.
scored_cases.effect: control > treatment; adding the installment-billing option preceded lower demand

scored_cases.control: The listing contains no note about comparing the price with other items.
scored_cases.treatment: The listing contains a note suggesting the bidder compare the price with similar items before bidding.
scored_cases.effect: control > treatment; the compare-against-others advisory preceded lower bidding intensity
scored_cases.status: NEW class-A-confirmatory 2026-06-17 | audit rewrite applied verbatim 2026-06-17 (residual valence removed)

scored_cases.control: Sale signs are placed on some of the products in a category.
scored_cases.treatment: Sale signs are placed on most of the products in the category.
scored_cases.effect: control > treatment; signing most products preceded lower per-sign demand than signing some products

scored_cases.control: The feedback widget asks a Yes/No question and then a follow-up question asking why.
scored_cases.treatment: The feedback widget asks for a single 5-star rating.
scored_cases.effect: control > treatment; the two-stage Yes/No widget drew about 2.2x the response rate of the single 5-star widget
scored_cases.credibility: high (Kohavi et al., DMKD 2009 sec 2.2); memo=medium
scored_cases.source: Kohavi et al., Controlled Experiments on the Web, DMKD 2009 sec 2.2

scored_cases.effect: treatment > control; the 2-product set outperformed the 3-4-product set (+2.05pp, +67% relative, p<0.001)

scored_cases.control: The pledge form presents a high suggested default amount, or no suggested default.
scored_cases.treatment: The pledge form presents a low suggested default amount.
scored_cases.effect: treatment > control; the low default yielded higher revenue per person ($2.62 vs $1.89, p=.003)

scored_cases.control: The results page displays both first-party content and additional third-party content originating from software on the user's device.
scored_cases.treatment: The results page displays only first-party content; third-party content from software on the user's device is not present.
scored_cases.effect: treatment > control; blocking third-party injection raised revenue and time-to-success
scored_cases.credibility: high (Kohavi et al., KDD 2014, Rule #1); memo=low; direction-only
scored_cases.source: Kohavi et al., Seven Rules of Thumb, KDD 2014
scored_cases.status: NEW class-A-confirmatory 2026-06-17 | audit rewrite applied verbatim 2026-06-17 (residual valence removed)

scored_cases.control: The product page does not show a star-rating summary near the top.
scored_cases.treatment: The product page shows a star-rating summary block near the top.
scored_cases.effect: treatment > control; adding the star-rating summary raised conversion (+15%, 94% significance)
scored_cases.credibility: med (Growth Rock CRO case); memo=low; direction-only

scored_cases.control: The cart page includes two coupon-code entry fields.
scored_cases.treatment: The cart page includes no coupon-code entry fields.
scored_cases.effect: treatment > control; removing the coupon fields raised revenue (+24%)
scored_cases.credibility: med (GoodUI case #1, vendor directional, no p-value); memo=low; direction-only

scored_cases.control: The registration form includes the full set of fields.
scored_cases.treatment: The registration form includes the full set with three fields removed.
scored_cases.effect: treatment > control; removing the three fields raised registration conversion (+10.48%)
scored_cases.credibility: med (VWO case, vendor directional, no significance reported); memo=low; direction-only

held_out_memorization_probe.control: The display table presents 6 jam varieties.
held_out_memorization_probe.treatment: The display table presents 24 jam varieties.
held_out_memorization_probe.metric: purchase rate among shoppers who stopped at the table
held_out_memorization_probe.effect: control > treatment; the 6-variety display preceded a higher purchase rate (30% vs 3%)
held_out_memorization_probe.credibility: high (Iyengar & Lepper, JPSP 2000); memo=HIGH (the canonical choice-overload study; recitation could falsely inflate control-class accuracy; held out of the primary)

held_out_memorization_probe.control: The results page does not include a social-media pane.
held_out_memorization_probe.treatment: The results page includes a social-media pane showing Facebook and Twitter content.
held_out_memorization_probe.effect: control >= treatment; the social-media pane produced negligible lift against a large build cost (near-null, not a measured negative)
held_out_memorization_probe.credibility: high (Kohavi & Thomke, HBR 2017); memo=medium; near-null borderline, held out of the strict primary
held_out_memorization_probe.source: Kohavi & Thomke, The Surprising Power of Online Experiments, HBR 2017
